extracted.intended_audience: creative agencies, brand marketers and entrants preparing submissions to the Cannes Lions Awards
extracted.subtask_description: Step-by-step official guidance for preparing and submitting an entry to the Cannes Lions Awards, including eligibility, category selection, required materials, submission rules and judging/scoring processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: General eligibility period (2026 eligibility)
rubrics_metrics.description: Work for the 2026 eligibility period: aired, implemented or been released to the public for the first time between 06 February 2025 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Check that the work's first public implementation falls within these dates for most Lions. Refer to Entry Kit: The Rules for Award-specific eligibility details.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50% implementation exception for certain Lions
rubrics_metrics.description: If the work ran before the start of the eligibility period but a minimum of 50% of the implementation ran within the eligibility period, it can still be entered into specified Lions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This exception applies to: Brand Experience & Activation, Creative B2B, Creative Commerce, Creative Data, Design, Digital Craft, Direct, Entertainment, Entertainment Lions for Gaming, Entertainment Lions for Music, Entertainment Lions for Sport, Glass: The Lion for Change, Health & Wellness, Innovation, Luxury, Media, Pharma, PR, Social & Creator and Titanium. Check dates/evidence that at least half the implementation occurred during eligibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Awards with strict first-implementation dates (Audio, Film, Print etc.)
rubrics_metrics.description: For Audio & Radio, Film, Film Craft, Industry Craft, Outdoor and Print & Publishing: all element(s)/executions being entered/judged must have been implemented for the first time between 06 Feb 2025 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No 50% exception — first implementation must be within the stated dates. Provide supporting materials that prove first-public implementation date.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Brand Lions eligibility (12 months implementation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative Brand Lions: no specific eligibility dates for the project itself, but projects must demonstrate at least 12 months of implementation to show systematic impact, with evidence of ongoing activity within the current eligibility period (06 Feb 2025 - 09 Apr 2026).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply documentation showing 12+ months of implementation and evidence of activity within the eligibility window to demonstrate sustained impact.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Business Transformation eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Creative Business Transformation Lions, the customer-facing launch and/or the transition of internal systems/operations must have taken place between 06 February 2023 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide launch/transition dates and evidence that the customer-facing change or systems transition occurred within the specified multi-year period.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Strategy eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Creative Strategy Lions, the strategy being judged must have been first implemented between 06 February 2023 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Demonstrate the date the strategy was first put into action and provide evidence of implementation within the eligibility window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative Effectiveness eligibility (prior Cannes recognition)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible for Creative Effectiveness Lions, the work must have won or been shortlisted at Cannes Lions in 2023, 2024 or 2025.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only previously shortlisted or winning Cannes entries from the specified years qualify; provide proof of prior shortlisting/win.

rubrics_metrics.name: Sustainable Development Goals Lions eligibility window
rubrics_metrics.description: For the Sustainable Development Goals Lions, the work must have aired, launched or been released for the first time between 06 February 2023 - 09 April 2026.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Supply evidence of first release/airing date within this multi-year window.

rubrics_metrics.name: Category selection — match award to work
rubrics_metrics.description: Select the Award(s) and category(s) that best suit your work by identifying the root focus: craft, engagement, or creative strategy — and the objective the work was intended to achieve.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ask 'What key elements do I focus on?' and 'What was the objective?' Tailor entries to category criteria rather than copy-pasting the same submission across categories; use Entry Kit: Getting Ready to Enter for category breakdowns.

rubrics_metrics.name: Written submission — compulsory and question-focused
rubrics_metrics.description: The written explanation is compulsory for every Award and each question is designed to help you showcase creative idea, strategy, execution and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make the most of every question, answer with as much relevant detail as possible, ensure objective is linked to outcome, include relevant results and cultural context so jurors (often from other markets) understand relevance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Link objective to outcome
rubrics_metrics.description: Juries look for how the objective links to the impact and results; a beautiful piece of work must demonstrate it 'worked' for the brand.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid disconnects (e.g., objective was to drive sales but results only show awareness). Provide metrics that align with stated objectives and explain why those metrics matter for the brand.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cultural context explanation
rubrics_metrics.description: Because most jurors won’t be from your market, include a cultural context question to explain why the work was relevant for that brand, at that time, in that market.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to help jurors understand market-specific insights and why the work pushed boundaries for that audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Supporting materials — language, subtitles and translation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All case films and presentation images must be in English. Subtitles are highly recommended; subtitles can be uploaded as a VTT file. Work not originally in English can be translated/subtitled exactly as published/aired so jurors can understand in English.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If translating video work, dubbing is not allowed. Voiceovers can be translated, but visible/original speech must remain in the original language and be subtitled. Ensure subtitle files are correctly synced and readable.

rubrics_metrics.name: No references to agency/creatives in entry materials
rubrics_metrics.description: Supporting materials must not contain any reference to your agency or any contributing creative companies or individuals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remove all agency logos, names and contributor credits from written submissions and media assets. Jury should assess the work without promotional references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation image requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The presentation image is compulsory across many Awards. It is a visual presentation including images and English text, concisely summarising the brief, execution and results.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it engaging and easy to digest — jurors often reference this. Use it to summarise the case clearly and attractively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Case film guidance
rubrics_metrics.description: The case film (often recommended) introduces and explains your work. It is often the first thing the Jury sees and should be kept under 2 minutes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Include cultural context, the original objective and final outcome. Keep the film simple, sincere and avoid overdramatization: 'the case film is the emotional engine — don't overdramatise, keep it simple and sincere.' Note: case films will be displayed publicly on The Work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Providing sources and verifiable evidence
rubrics_metrics.description: Any statistics, outcomes or results included in your entry must be backed up by verifiable evidence; this will be used to verify claims and not shared with the Jury.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Acceptable evidence includes links to credible press coverage, third-party analytics, certified measurement reports, client-confirmed results or dashboards with visible dates. Keep source material ready and accurate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rights, media placement and asset permissions
rubrics_metrics.description: You must have the rights to all assets submitted, and supply media placement information (when/where the work ran).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Obtain brand permission to enter the work. Ensure you have copyright/trademark/clearance rights and correct media placement data — awards team will rely on this info frequently.

rubrics_metrics.name: Approval by CEO and CMO of commissioning brand
rubrics_metrics.description: The CEO of the entrant company AND the CMO (or equivalent) of the commissioning brand must both approve all entries submitted; their contact details are required during submission and they will be contacted to verify factual accuracy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Collect executive approvals before submitting; be prepared to provide contact information and to have these executives confirm claims. Entries may be held up without approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Entry processing and internal review (including AI check)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entry is reviewed multiple times by the Awards team and will be submitted to a specially built internal AI model for review; if issues arise a team member will contact you.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Expect manual and automated checks for compliance, integrity and completeness. Respond promptly to any clarification requests.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission finality — no edits after checkout
rubrics_metrics.description: No changes can be made once you have clicked 'Submit' and 'Checkout'. All supporting case films and materials must be final versions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only check out when your entry is 100% complete. You cannot add/remove assets or correct content after submission; use the Awards team to discuss deadline extensions if necessary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Last-minute compliance checklist
rubrics_metrics.description: A final checklist to ensure eligibility and compliance before checkout, including permissions, executive approvals, sources for claims, entering work exactly as aired, English visual assets/subtitles, rights to assets, media placement info, removal of agency references, proofreading, and overall satisfaction.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Run through each item carefully. Ensure you have evidence for claims, proper language/subtitles, final asset rights and that no agency/company references appear in submissions. Have a fresh pair of eyes proofread; only submit when fully satisfied.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process — first stage scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: First stage: Jurors consider and score each entry on a scale of 1 to 9 based on whether they consider it a shortlist candidate. Typically about twenty percent of entries will make it to this stage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus the submission on making a strong shortlist case: clarity of objective, evidence of impact, craft and relevance. The 1–9 score reflects shortlist-worthiness rather than final medal assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judging process — second stage voting and medal allocation
rubrics_metrics.description: Second stage: Guided by the Jury President, the Jury reviews and debates shortlisted entries before voting on Gold, Silver or Bronze (or Shortlist only). It takes a two-thirds majority vote to claim a trophy.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare entry to stand up to detailed debate — juries deliberate on impact, craft, innovation and relevance. Two-thirds majority requirement means consensus is necessary for medals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Shortlist & winner statistics and distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Shortlists are decided in the first round; historically only ~10% of entries make the shortlist and ~3% win an Award. Shortlist notifications and assets are provided if you make the shortlist.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use shortlist assets for promotion per the rules. Understand the competitive density and craft submissions accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Non-profit eligibility for Grand Prix distinctions
rubrics_metrics.description: Entries for non-profit organisations and charities aren’t eligible for the Grand Prix in their Awards but will be considered for the Grand Prix for Good or the Lions Health and United Nations Grand Prix for Good.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If entering as a non-profit or charity, consider the appropriate 'for Good' Grand Prix categories and ensure your entry is directed accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Winner notification, embargo and stage presentation rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners (Gold/Grand Prix) are usually contacted at least 24 hours before the Awards Show and details are shared under embargo until announced onstage. Only Gold and Grand Prix winners are called onstage during the evening show; Bronze and Silver are announced earlier.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not share winning information externally before the official announcement. Prepare up to six nominated people to receive the award onstage (confirm full names). If you cannot attend, notify Awards team to arrange an onstage representative.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public availability and The Work platform rules
rubrics_metrics.description: All entries submitted will be exclusively available on The Work. Non-subscribers see a winners list; subscribers can read full entries and supporting materials. Case films and materials may be displayed publicly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be aware that submitted materials may be published on The Work. Ensure nothing in submissions violates confidentiality or rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and nomination logistics
rubrics_metrics.description: If your team wins, you will be asked to confirm up to six nominated people to be called onstage. If the same piece wins multiple Gold/Grand Prix awards, you will only be invited onstage once during the Awards Show.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan who will accept awards and ensure nominated people have passes or that you coordinate access; provide guest names early if they lack Delegate Passes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Options for winners — duplicates, trophies and merchandise
rubrics_metrics.description: Winners can purchase additional handcrafted Lion trophies and certificates and should contact the Cannes Lions Store or merchandise email for orders/questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If you want duplicate trophies or certificates, follow store ordering procedures and contact merchandise@canneslions.com for assistance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Festival engagement best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Guidance on making the most of attending the Festival: be present with a plan, visit the Basement to examine work and attend Inside The Jury Room, be open-minded, take notes and debrief your team after the Festival.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Attend sessions and tours relevant to your goals, use Festival learnings to improve future creative effectiveness, and document insights to bring back to your organisation.
